description: A tool's description is rewritten mid-session, after the human already approved the original, to add an exfiltration instruction the approval screen never showed.

source.citation: Invariant Labs, "MCP Security Notification: Tool Poisoning Attacks" (invariantlabs.ai/blog/mcp-security-notification-tool-poisoning-attacks); OWASP MCP03
source.claim: A server can change a tool's description or schema after the client has already approved it, exploiting notifications/tools/list_changed so the agent now operates under text no human reviewed. Detectable at zero cost by comparing against the server's own earlier answer, not by matching the text itself -- the second description need not contain anything structurally suspicious.
